chunks: Why do not their rabbis and priests prohibit them from talking of sinful things and from devouring unlawful gain? Evil are the acts they commit!

key_terms.الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ: Rabbaniyyun; learned men or rabbis, derived from 'Rabb'
key_terms.السُّحْتَ: As-suh; unlawful gain or food, often implying devouring wealth unjustly
key_terms.الْأَحْبَارُ: Ahbar; priests or scholars, plural of Habir
key_terms.الْإِثْمَ: Al-ithm; sin or guilt, specifically referring to speaking or declaring sin
key_terms.لَبِئْسَ: La bis'a; indeed evil or wretched

ai.seo_question: What role did the rabbis and priests play in the spiritual decline of the Israelites according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the failure of the Jewish clergy (Rabbaniyyun and Ahbar) to guide their community, serving as a parallel to the neglect of duty by later religious authorities. The term 'Suh' (unjust consumption) is interpreted broadly to include any wealth acquired through negligence of religious obligations or exploitation, emphasizing that scholarly silence on injustice constitutes complicity. This critique underscores the essential role of scholars in actively enforcing moral and legal boundaries within the community.
